items.source: With the Old Breed (Eugene Sledge); Helmet for My Pillow (Robert Leckie)

items.title: The Paper Chase
items.plot: James Hart, a first-year student at a prestigious law school, struggles under the demanding contract-law professor Charles Kingsfield. He and his study group deal with heavy workloads, ambition and romance.
items.source: The Paper Chase (John Jay Osborn Jr.) and the 1973 film

items.title: The Phil Silvers Show
items.plot: Master Sergeant Ernie Bilko, a fast-talking con man who runs the motor pool at a sleepy Kansas army post, cooks up get-rich-quick schemes and outwits his gullible colonel with help from his loyal platoon.

won: 1957 · Best Series – Half Hour or Less

items.title: The Philco Television Playhouse
items.plot: A landmark live anthology of hour-long dramas that showcased new television writers such as Paddy Chayefsky, Horton Foote and Gore Vidal. It started with stage and book adaptations and later turned to intimate original plays such as Marty.

items.title: The Philco-Goodyear Television Playhouse
items.plot: From 1951 the Philco Television Playhouse alternated weeks with the Goodyear Television Playhouse in the same Sunday slot. Together they offered live original dramas by writers such as Paddy Chayefsky, Horton Foote and Tad Mosel, including Marty.

items.title: The Pillars of the Earth
items.plot: In 12th-century England, torn apart by a civil war over the crown, master builder Tom and the devout Prior Philip set out to build a great cathedral in Kingsbridge. Scheming nobles and churchmen threaten their work.
items.source: The Pillars of the Earth (Ken Follett)

items.title: The Practice
items.plot: Idealistic defense attorney Bobby Donnell and his small Boston law firm take on ethically difficult criminal and civil cases. They often defend people they suspect are guilty, while struggling to keep the firm afloat.

won: 1999 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
nominated: 2000 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2001 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: The Red Skelton Show
items.plot: A long-running comedy-variety hour led by clown and comedian Red Skelton. He played a gallery of recurring characters such as Freddie the Freeloader and Clem Kadiddlehopper in sketches, pantomimes and musical numbers, and closed with his trademark "Good night, and may God bless."

nominated: 1960 · Outstanding Program Achievement in the Field of Humor
1962 · Outstanding Program Achievement in the Field of Humor

items.title: The Richard Boone Show
items.plot: A drama anthology performed by a permanent repertory company led by Richard Boone. The same actors played new roles each week in original teleplays, with playwright Clifford Odets as the original story editor.

nominated: 1964 · Outstanding Program Achievement in the Field of Drama

won: 1964 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: The Rockford Files
items.plot: Jim Rockford, a laid-back ex-con pardoned for a crime he didn't commit, works as a private investigator out of a trailer in Malibu. He takes cases the police won't touch, often gets beaten up and rarely gets paid.

nominated: 1980 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: The Scarlett O'Hara War
items.plot: Producer David O. Selznick runs a frantic, star-studded search for the actress to play Scarlett O'Hara in Gone with the Wind, as Hollywood's leading ladies compete for the part. It was part of the Moviola miniseries.

items.title: The Six Wives of Henry VIII
items.plot: Six plays, each told from the point of view of one of Henry VIII's wives, from Catherine of Aragon to Catherine Parr. Together they trace the king's journey from a dashing young prince to an ailing, paranoid tyrant.

items.title: The Starter Wife
items.plot: Molly Kagan, the wife of a Hollywood studio executive, is dumped for a younger woman. She has to rebuild her life and identity outside the shallow world of Los Angeles power wives, with help from her witty friends.

items.title: The Streets of San Francisco
items.plot: Veteran homicide detective Mike Stone teams with his young, college-educated partner Steve Keller to solve murders and other crimes, shot on location across San Francisco.

nominated: 1975 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: The Studio
items.plot: Matt Remick, a film-loving executive, finally becomes head of a struggling Hollywood studio. He finds the job means balancing his artistic ideals against corporate demands, fragile stars and directors, and one cringe-worthy crisis after another.

won: 2026 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy

items.title: The Temptations
items.plot: Narrated by founding member Otis Williams, this biopic follows the Motown vocal group from the streets of Detroit to stardom. It covers the hits as well as the egos, addictions and lineup changes that strained the group.

items.title: The Thorn Birds
items.plot: On a vast Australian sheep station, Meggie Cleary loves the ambitious priest Ralph de Bricassart from girlhood. Over decades their forbidden love pulls against his rise in the Catholic Church.

items.title: The Two Mrs. Grenvilles
items.plot: A showgirl marries into a wealthy old-money New York family, to the disapproval of her powerful mother-in-law. When she fatally shoots her husband and claims she mistook him for a prowler, the family closes ranks.

items.title: The Underground Railroad
items.plot: Cora, enslaved on a Georgia plantation, escapes north on an Underground Railroad that is an actual network of secret trains. Each state she reaches shows a different form of American cruelty, and a relentless slave catcher pursues her.

setting.place: Georgia, South Carolina, Tennessee, Indiana and beyond

items.title: The United States Steel Hour
items.plot: A prestigious live anthology produced by the Theatre Guild and sponsored by U.S. Steel. It presented original teleplays and stage adaptations with leading actors of the day, as well as early work by many future stars.

items.title: The Untouchables
items.plot: During Prohibition, federal agent Eliot Ness and his incorruptible squad battle Chicago's gangsters, bootleggers and racketeers with raids and shootouts, narrated in a clipped newsreel style by Walter Winchell.
items.source: The Untouchables (Eliot Ness and Oscar Fraley memoir)

nominated: 1960 · Outstanding Program Achievement in the Field of Drama
1961 · Outstanding Program Achievement in the Field of Drama

items.title: The Waltons
items.plot: Narrated by the adult John-Boy, the series follows a close-knit, three-generation family that runs a lumber mill in rural Virginia through the Great Depression and World War II, while John-Boy dreams of becoming a writer.
items.source: Spencer's Mountain (Earl Hamner Jr.) and The Homecoming (1971 TV film)

won: 1974 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
nominated: 1973 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
1975 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: The White Lotus
items.plot: A satirical anthology set over one week at a luxury White Lotus resort, where wealthy guests and stressed staff clash over privilege, sex and money. Each season opens with a death and moves to a new location: Hawaii, Sicily, Thailand.

nominated: 2026 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: The White Queen
items.plot: During the Wars of the Roses, commoner Elizabeth Woodville secretly marries Edward IV of York. She schemes against rival women, Margaret Beaufort and Anne Neville, as the houses of York and Lancaster fight for the English throne.

items.title: The White Shadow
items.plot: After a knee injury ends his NBA career, Ken Reeves becomes basketball coach at a racially mixed inner-city Los Angeles high school. He guides his players through games and through serious problems off the court.

items.title: The Winds of War
items.plot: Naval officer Victor "Pug" Henry becomes an informal envoy for President Roosevelt as World War II begins, meeting Hitler, Churchill and Stalin. Meanwhile his family is scattered across Europe and the Pacific, ending with the attack on Pearl Harbor.

items.title: The Women of Brewster Place
items.plot: Seven African-American women living in a run-down housing block on a dead-end urban street face poverty, heartbreak, violence and prejudice, and lean on one another for strength.
items.source: The Women of Brewster Place (Gloria Naylor)

items.title: The Wonder Years
items.plot: The adult Kevin Arnold looks back on growing up in the suburbs from 1968 to 1973: family tensions, his best friend Paul, his on-and-off romance with Winnie Cooper and the turbulent backdrop of the era.

won: 1989 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
nominated: 1990 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy

items.title: Three's Company
items.plot: To share a Santa Monica apartment with two single women, Jack Tripper pretends to be gay to satisfy their prudish landlord. Misunderstandings and double entendres follow.

nominated: 1979 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy

items.title: Tin Man
items.plot: Small-town waitress DG is swept into the O.Z., a dark sci-fi version of Oz ruled by a tyrannical sorceress. With a former cop called the Tin Man, a brain-damaged Glitch and the shape-shifter Raw, she uncovers her own royal past.
items.source: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (L. Frank Baum)

items.title: Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy
items.plot: George Smiley, a retired British intelligence officer, is quietly called back to find a Soviet mole at the top of the Circus. He patiently works through old files, betrayed agents and the senior officers he once worked with.
items.source: Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy (John le Carré)

items.title: To Serve Them All My Days
items.plot: Welsh miner's son David Powlett-Jones comes home shell-shocked from the trenches of World War I and takes a teaching post at a West Country boys' school. Over two decades he finds healing, love and his calling there.
items.source: To Serve Them All My Days (R. F. Delderfield)

items.title: Tom Brown's Schooldays
items.plot: Young Tom Brown arrives at Rugby School under the reforming headmaster Dr. Thomas Arnold. He makes friends, takes on the cruel bully Flashman and gradually grows into a principled young man.

items.title: Too Big to Fail
items.plot: As Lehman Brothers collapses in September 2008, Treasury Secretary Hank Paulson and Fed officials race through tense negotiations with Wall Street CEOs to keep the financial system from falling apart.
items.source: Too Big to Fail (Andrew Ross Sorkin)

items.title: Top of the Lake
items.plot: Detective Robin Griffin returns to her remote New Zealand hometown to investigate the disappearance of a pregnant 12-year-old, and confronts the town's violent patriarch and her own past. A second season moves to Sydney and a new case.

items.title: Topper
items.plot: Stuffy banker Cosmo Topper moves into a house haunted by its former owners, a fun-loving young couple killed in an avalanche, and their brandy-drinking dog. Only Topper can see them, and they set out to loosen him up.

items.title: Traffic
items.plot: Interwoven stories follow the global trade in drugs, guns and people: a DEA agent in Seattle, a migrant smuggling operation, and an Afghan farmer pulled into the heroin trade. The series shows how these illegal networks connect across borders.

items.title: Transparent
items.plot: When retired professor Mort Pfefferman comes out to her adult children as transgender woman Maura, the self-absorbed Los Angeles family is forced to reckon with identity, sexuality and secrets across generations.

won: 2015 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
nominated: 2016 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
2017 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy

items.title: Treme
items.plot: Three months after Hurricane Katrina, New Orleans musicians, chefs, Mardi Gras Indians and ordinary residents try to rebuild their lives and their city's culture amid official neglect, corruption and crime.

items.title: True Blood
items.plot: Synthetic blood has let vampires come out publicly. In a small Louisiana town, telepathic waitress Sookie Stackhouse falls for the vampire Bill Compton and is drawn into a world of vampires, shapeshifters, werewolves and fairies.

nominated: 2009 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2010 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: Two and a Half Men
items.plot: Hedonistic jingle writer Charlie Harper's Malibu beach house is invaded by his uptight divorced brother Alan and Alan's son Jake. Later a heartbroken internet billionaire buys the house and joins the household.

items.title: Ugly Betty
items.plot: Betty Suarez, a kind-hearted but unfashionable young Mexican-American woman from Queens, lands a job as assistant to the playboy editor of a glossy Manhattan fashion magazine. There she faces snobbery and scheming while chasing her dreams.

won: 2007 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy

items.title: Unbelievable
items.plot: A teenager in Washington State reports being raped and is pressured into recanting, then charged with lying. Years later, two female detectives in Colorado link a series of similar attacks and hunt a serial rapist.
items.source: An Unbelievable Story of Rape (T. Christian Miller and Ken Armstrong, ProPublica/The Marshall Project)

items.title: Unbreakable Kimmy Schmidt
items.plot: After 15 years in an underground doomsday cult's bunker, relentlessly optimistic Kimmy Schmidt moves to New York City. She rooms with a struggling gay actor and works for a self-absorbed socialite while catching up on the modern world.

items.title: Unorthodox
items.plot: A 19-year-old woman flees her arranged marriage and the ultra-Orthodox Satmar community of Williamsburg, Brooklyn, for Berlin, where she makes new friends and dares to audition for a music conservatory. Meanwhile her husband and his volatile cousin are sent to find her and bring her home.
items.source: Unorthodox: The Scandalous Rejection of My Hasidic Roots (Deborah Feldman memoir)

items.title: Upstairs, Downstairs
items.plot: The lives of the wealthy Bellamy family and their servants at 165 Eaton Place in London intertwine over three decades, from the Edwardian era through the First World War and into the late 1920s, as social change slowly reshapes both floors of the house.

won: 1975 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
nominated: 1978 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: Veep
items.plot: Selina Meyer, a vain and ambitious US Vice President, schemes for relevance and power alongside a staff of bickering, incompetent aides, stumbling from one public-relations disaster to the next as she chases the presidency.

nominated: 2016 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
2017 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy

items.title: WKRP in Cincinnati
items.plot: A new program director switches a struggling Cincinnati radio station from elevator music to rock and roll, to the dismay of its bumbling station manager, and gathers an eccentric staff of DJs, salesmen and newsmen.

items.title: Wagon Train
items.plot: A wagon master and his scout lead settlers on the long trek from Missouri to California after the Civil War. Each week focuses on a different traveler or encounter along the trail, often with a guest star.

nominated: 1958 · Best Dramatic Series with Continuing Characters

items.title: WandaVision
items.plot: Wanda Maximoff and Vision live an idyllic suburban life that shifts through the styles of classic TV sitcoms decade by decade, until cracks in their picture-perfect reality hint that something is very wrong in the town of Westview.

items.title: War and Remembrance
items.plot: Continuing The Winds of War, naval officer Victor 'Pug' Henry and his family are scattered across the globe during World War II, from the Pacific naval battles to Washington, while his Jewish daughter-in-law and her uncle are trapped in Nazi-occupied Europe and the Holocaust.

items.title: Washington: Behind Closed Doors
items.plot: A paranoid, power-hungry president and his inner circle maneuver against rivals, the press and the CIA, drawing the White House into secret surveillance and cover-ups. A thinly veiled fictional account of the Nixon era drawn from a Watergate figure's novel.

items.title: Watchmen
items.plot: In an alternate 2019 where masked vigilantes are outlawed and Tulsa police hide their faces, detective Angela Abar investigates a white-supremacist group's attack and uncovers buried secrets linking her family history to the 1921 Tulsa race massacre and the original Watchmen.

items.title: Wednesday
items.plot: Deadpan Wednesday Addams is sent to Nevermore Academy, a boarding school for outcasts, where she tries to master her emerging psychic visions while investigating a string of monstrous killings tied to the school and her family's past.

nominated: 2023 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy

items.title: Weeds
items.plot: After her husband dies suddenly, suburban mother Nancy Botwin starts dealing marijuana to keep up her family's comfortable lifestyle, and her business grows into ever more dangerous entanglements with rival dealers, cartels and the law.

nominated: 2006 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
2007 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
2009 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy

items.title: Welcome Back, Kotter
items.plot: Gabe Kotter returns to the Brooklyn high school he once attended to teach a remedial class of wisecracking troublemakers known as the Sweathogs, using humor and his own street smarts to reach them.

items.title: Westworld
items.plot: In a futuristic Wild West theme park, wealthy guests indulge any fantasy with lifelike android hosts. When some hosts begin to remember past cycles and question their reality, an awakening begins that spills beyond the park into the human world.

setting.place: Western theme park and future cities

nominated: 2017 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: Widow's Bay
items.plot: The skeptical mayor of a small, eerie New England island town tries to bring in tourists and modernize the place, refusing to believe residents' warnings that the town is cursed, until strange and terrifying events suggest the locals may be right.

items.title: Will & Grace
items.plot: Gay lawyer Will and his straight best friend Grace, an interior designer, share a Manhattan apartment and a co-dependent friendship, joined by Will's flamboyant friend Jack and Grace's boozy socialite assistant Karen.

nominated: 2000 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
2001 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
2002 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
2003 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
2004 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
2005 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
2018 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy

items.title: Wiseguy
items.plot: Undercover federal agent Vinnie Terranova infiltrates organized crime syndicates, crooked businesses and other criminal networks in multi-episode story arcs, struggling to keep his identity and his conscience intact.

nominated: 1989 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
1990 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: Wolf Hall
items.plot: Thomas Cromwell, a blacksmith's son turned lawyer, rises to become Henry VIII's most powerful adviser, engineering the king's break with Rome and the downfall of Anne Boleyn, while the shifting politics of the Tudor court make his position ever more precarious.

items.title: World War II: When Lions Roared
items.plot: A dramatization of the wartime alliance between Franklin D. Roosevelt, Winston Churchill and Joseph Stalin, tracing their strained cooperation, rivalries and summit negotiations as they steer the Allies through World War II.

setting.place: Washington, London, Moscow and summit sites

items.title: Yellowjackets
items.plot: In 1996 a New Jersey high-school girls' soccer team survives a plane crash in the remote Canadian wilderness and descends into savagery. Twenty-five years later, the survivors find the dark secrets of what they did to stay alive returning to haunt them.

items.title: You Bet Your Life
items.plot: Groucho Marx hosts a quiz show where pairs of contestants answer questions for prize money, but the real attraction is Groucho's ad-libbed banter and insults during the interviews, plus the chance to say the 'secret word' for a bonus.

items.title: Your Friends & Neighbors
items.plot: After losing his job and facing an expensive divorce, a disgraced hedge-fund manager starts secretly stealing from the luxurious homes of his wealthy neighbors to keep up appearances, uncovering their secrets and getting pulled into a dangerous crime along the way.

items.title: thirtysomething
items.plot: A circle of baby-boomer friends in Philadelphia navigate marriage, parenthood, careers, friendship and the anxieties of approaching middle age, centered on advertising partners Michael and Elliot and their families.

won: 1989 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
nominated: 1988 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
1990 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
1991 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: The Twilight Zone
items.plot: Rod Serling introduces self-contained tales in which ordinary people stumble into strange situations involving the supernatural, science fiction or psychological terror, often ending with an ironic twist and a moral sting.

nominated: 1961 · Outstanding Program Achievement in the Field of Drama

items.title: The Bugs Bunny Show
items.plot: Bugs Bunny hosts a showcase of classic Warner Bros. Looney Tunes and Merrie Melodies cartoons, tied together with newly animated linking segments featuring Bugs, Daffy Duck and the rest of the gang. The package ran in prime time, then for decades on Saturday mornings.

items.title: Mister Rogers' Neighborhood
items.plot: Gentle host Fred Rogers speaks directly to young viewers about feelings, kindness and everyday life, visits real workplaces, and leads a trolley ride to the puppet-populated Neighborhood of Make-Believe.

setting.place: Pittsburgh studio and the Neighborhood of Make-Believe

items.title: Monty Python's Flying Circus
items.plot: A surreal sketch comedy show from the Monty Python troupe, stringing together absurd skits, stream-of-consciousness transitions and Terry Gilliam's cut-out animations, while gleefully mocking British institutions and TV conventions.

items.title: El Chavo
items.plot: A poor, hungry orphan boy who hides in a barrel in a Mexico City tenement courtyard gets into constant mischief with the neighborhood kids and the exasperated adults, including the landlord, the widow next door and the schoolteacher.

items.title: The World at War
items.plot: A landmark documentary history of the Second World War, told through archival footage and interviews with leaders, soldiers and civilians from all sides, from the rise of Nazi Germany to the atomic bombings and the war's aftermath.

items.title: Fawlty Towers
items.plot: Rude, snobbish hotelier Basil Fawlty runs a seaside hotel in Torquay with his domineering wife Sybil, sensible maid Polly and hapless Spanish waiter Manuel, as his schemes and lies spiral into farcical disasters.

items.title: I, Claudius
items.plot: The aging Emperor Claudius recounts the poisonings, plots and scandals of the Julio-Claudian dynasty, from Augustus and his scheming wife Livia through Tiberius and the mad Caligula, surviving by being underestimated as a stammering fool.
items.source: I, Claudius and Claudius the God (Robert Graves)

items.title: Mind Your Language
items.plot: An English teacher takes on an evening class of adult foreign students from around the world at a London college, where misunderstandings, mangled grammar and cultural clashes cause constant comic chaos under a stern principal.

items.title: Cosmos
items.plot: Astronomer Carl Sagan guides viewers aboard his 'Ship of the Imagination' through the history of science and the universe, from the origins of life and the evolution of stars to humanity's place in the cosmos.

items.title: Yes Minister
items.plot: Newly appointed Cabinet minister Jim Hacker tries to push through reforms, but his wily Permanent Secretary Sir Humphrey Appleby uses every bureaucratic trick to keep the civil service in control, with private secretary Bernard caught in between.

items.title: Only Fools and Horses
items.plot: Market trader Del Boy Trotter and his younger brother Rodney scrape by in a Peckham tower block, selling dodgy goods and chasing get-rich-quick schemes in the belief that 'this time next year, we'll be millionaires.'

items.title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
items.plot: Brilliant, eccentric detective Sherlock Holmes and his loyal companion Dr. Watson solve baffling cases in Victorian London, in faithful adaptations of Arthur Conan Doyle's stories ending with Holmes's confrontation with Moriarty.

items.title: Das Boot
items.plot: The crew of German U-boat U-96 endures cramped quarters, boredom, depth-charge attacks and terror on a 1941 patrol in the Atlantic, in the extended television version of Wolfgang Petersen's acclaimed submarine war film.

items.title: Blackadder II
items.plot: In the court of Queen Elizabeth I, the scheming, sarcastic Lord Edmund Blackadder tries to win the favor of the childish queen while fending off rivals and dealing with his dim servant Baldrick and the idiotic Lord Percy.

items.title: Dragon Ball
items.plot: Goku, a monkey-tailed boy of incredible strength, joins the inventive Bulma on a quest to gather the seven wish-granting Dragon Balls, then trains in martial arts, enters tournaments and battles villains while making lifelong friends.

items.title: The Return of Sherlock Holmes
items.plot: Sherlock Holmes returns after his presumed death at Reichenbach Falls and resumes solving mysteries in Victorian London with his friend Dr. Watson, in faithful adaptations of Conan Doyle's later stories.

items.title: Yes, Prime Minister
items.plot: Jim Hacker has unexpectedly become Prime Minister, but Sir Humphrey Appleby, now Cabinet Secretary, still manipulates him at every turn to protect the civil service, while Bernard tries to stay loyal to both.

items.title: Blackadder the Third
items.plot: In Regency England, the cunning Mr. E. Blackadder serves as butler to the spectacularly dim Prince George, trying to profit from his master's stupidity while dodging disasters with the help of his ever-filthy dogsbody Baldrick.

items.title: Ramayan
items.plot: A retelling of the Hindu epic: Prince Rama is exiled from Ayodhya for fourteen years, and when the demon king Ravana abducts his wife Sita, Rama, his brother Lakshmana and the devoted Hanuman wage war to rescue her.

items.title: Star Trek: The Next Generation
items.plot: A century after Kirk's era, Captain Jean-Luc Picard commands the starship Enterprise-D on a mission of exploration and diplomacy, encountering new species, moral dilemmas and threats such as the Borg and the godlike Q.

items.title: Mahabharat
items.plot: An adaptation of the Hindu epic chronicling the bitter rivalry between the Pandava and Kaurava cousins over the throne of Hastinapur, guided by Lord Krishna and culminating in the great war at Kurukshetra.

items.title: Mystery Science Theater 3000
items.plot: A man trapped on a satellite by mad scientists is forced to watch terrible B-movies, and survives by cracking jokes at the screen alongside his homemade robot companions, whose silhouettes heckle each film.

items.title: Blackadder Goes Forth
items.plot: On the Western Front in 1917, Captain Edmund Blackadder schemes desperately to avoid being sent over the top, stuck in a trench with idealistic Lieutenant George and Private Baldrick under the blithely incompetent General Melchett.

items.title: Dekalog
items.plot: Ten hour-long films, each loosely inspired by one of the Ten Commandments, follow residents of a Warsaw housing estate facing moral and existential dilemmas about life, death, love, faith and truth.

items.title: Dragon Ball Z
items.plot: Now a grown man, Goku learns he is a Saiyan, a member of a warrior alien race, and with his friends and son Gohan defends Earth against ever more powerful foes such as Vegeta, Frieza, Cell and Majin Buu.

items.title: Lonesome Dove
items.plot: Two retired Texas Rangers, the easygoing Gus McCrae and the stern Woodrow Call, lead a cattle drive from the Mexican border to Montana, facing outlaws, storms and loss along the epic journey.

items.title: Poirot
items.plot: Fastidious Belgian detective Hercule Poirot uses his 'little grey cells' to solve murders among the British upper classes in the 1930s, often aided by Captain Hastings, Chief Inspector Japp and his secretary Miss Lemon.
items.source: Hercule Poirot novels and stories (Agatha Christie)

items.title: Seinfeld
items.plot: Stand-up comic Jerry Seinfeld and his self-absorbed friends George, Elaine and Kramer obsess over the trivial minutiae of everyday life in New York City, in a famously 'show about nothing.'

setting.place: Upper West Side, New York City

won: 1994 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
nominated: 1995 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
1996 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
1997 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
1998 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy

items.title: The Simpsons
items.plot: The misadventures of a working-class family in the town of Springfield: bumbling father Homer, patient mother Marge, troublemaking Bart, gifted Lisa and baby Maggie, in a long-running satire of American life and pop culture.

nominated: 2003 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy

items.title: Mr. Bean
items.plot: Childlike, nearly silent oddball Mr. Bean tackles everyday tasks like shopping, exams and church services with bizarre, self-centered solutions, causing slapstick chaos with his teddy bear and little Mini.

items.title: The Civil War
items.plot: Ken Burns's documentary chronicles the American Civil War through period photographs, letters, diaries and expert commentary, from the causes of secession through the major battles to Lincoln's assassination and the war's legacy.

items.title: Twin Peaks
items.plot: FBI Special Agent Dale Cooper arrives in a quirky Pacific Northwest logging town to investigate the murder of homecoming queen Laura Palmer, uncovering the townspeople's secrets and a malevolent supernatural presence in the woods.

won: 1991 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: Batman: The Animated Series
items.plot: In a moody, art-deco Gotham City, Batman battles crime and a gallery of complex villains, from the Joker and Two-Face to a tragic Mr. Freeze, aided by Alfred, Robin and Commissioner Gordon.

items.title: Homicide: Life on the Street
items.plot: Detectives in the Baltimore Police Department's homicide unit work the city's murders, wrestling with interrogations, politics, unsolved cases and the moral toll of the job, in a gritty and realistic portrait of police work.
items.source: Homicide: A Year on the Killing Streets (David Simon)

items.title: Tash Ma Tash
items.plot: A landmark Saudi satirical comedy in which its two stars play different characters in each self-contained episode, poking fun at social issues, bureaucracy, religious extremism and everyday life in Saudi Arabia.

items.title: The X-Files
items.plot: FBI agents Fox Mulder, a believer in the paranormal, and Dana Scully, a skeptical scientist, investigate unexplained cases while uncovering a vast government conspiracy to hide the truth about alien existence.

setting.place: Washington, D.C. and across the US

won: 1995 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
1997 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
1998 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
nominated: 1999 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: Friends
items.plot: Six friends in their twenties and thirties navigate love, careers and the ups and downs of adulthood in Manhattan, spending much of their time in each other's apartments and at the Central Perk coffeehouse.

nominated: 1996 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
1997 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
1998 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
2002 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
2003 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy

items.title: Dragon Ball
items.plot: English-dubbed version of the anime: monkey-tailed boy Goku teams up with Bulma to hunt for the seven wish-granting Dragon Balls, then trains in martial arts, competes in tournaments and battles villains with his friends.

items.title: Father Ted
items.plot: Three disgraced Catholic priests, the scheming Father Ted, the childlike Father Dougal and the drunken Father Jack, live in exile on remote Craggy Island with their tea-obsessed housekeeper Mrs. Doyle.

items.title: Neon Genesis Evangelion
items.plot: Fourteen-year-old Shinji Ikari is recruited by his estranged father to pilot a giant bio-mechanical Evangelion against mysterious beings called Angels attacking Tokyo-3, as the war exposes the deep psychological wounds of everyone involved.

items.title: Pride and Prejudice
items.plot: Spirited Elizabeth Bennet, one of five unmarried sisters, clashes with the proud, wealthy Mr. Darcy, and both must overcome misjudgments, family embarrassments and class barriers before recognizing their feelings.

items.title: The Beatles Anthology
items.plot: The Beatles tell their own story, from their Liverpool childhoods and Hamburg club days through Beatlemania, studio innovation and their 1970 breakup, using rare archival footage and new interviews with Paul, George and Ringo.

setting.place: Liverpool, Hamburg, London and world tours

items.title: Dragon Ball Z
items.plot: English-dubbed version of the anime: grown-up Goku discovers he is an alien Saiyan and, with his son Gohan and allies, defends Earth from increasingly powerful enemies like Vegeta, Frieza, Cell and Majin Buu.

items.title: Berserk
items.plot: In a brutal medieval fantasy world, lone mercenary Guts joins the Band of the Hawk led by the charismatic Griffith, rising through bloody wars until Griffith's ambition leads to a horrifying betrayal.

items.title: Brass Eye
items.plot: A savage parody of sensationalist current-affairs TV in which a pompous presenter tackles moral panics such as drugs, crime and animals, tricking real celebrities and politicians into endorsing absurd fake campaigns.

items.title: I'm Alan Partridge
items.plot: Socially inept broadcaster Alan Partridge, his chat show cancelled, lives in a roadside hotel and then a static caravan while hosting a graveyard-shift local radio show in Norwich and pitching desperate TV ideas.
items.source: Knowing Me, Knowing You... with Alan Partridge

items.title: Oz
items.plot: Inside Emerald City, an experimental unit of the Oswald State Penitentiary, inmates split into gangs of Muslims, Aryans, Latinos, Italians and others fight for power and survival while idealistic staff try to keep order.

items.title: South Park
items.plot: Four foul-mouthed fourth-graders, Stan, Kyle, Cartman and Kenny, have bizarre adventures in their small Colorado mountain town, in a crudely animated, fast-turnaround satire of current events, celebrities and American culture.

items.title: Cowboy Bebop
items.plot: In 2071, a ragtag crew of bounty hunters aboard the spaceship Bebop chases criminals across a colonized solar system, while laid-back Spike Spiegel's past in a crime syndicate slowly catches up with him.

items.title: Whose Line Is It Anyway?
items.plot: A host hands out arbitrary points while a panel of improv comedians performs games and scenes made up on the spot from audience suggestions and prop challenges.

items.title: Freaks and Geeks
items.plot: At a Michigan high school in 1980, honor student Lindsay Weir falls in with a crowd of burnouts while her younger brother Sam and his nerdy friends try to survive freshman year.

items.title: One Piece
items.plot: Rubber-bodied Monkey D. Luffy sets out to sea with a growing crew of misfit pirates, searching for the legendary treasure One Piece to become King of the Pirates while battling rival pirates and the World Government.

items.title: Spaced
items.plot: Two twentysomething strangers, aspiring comic artist Tim and would-be writer Daisy, pose as a couple to rent a London flat, and their aimless lives become surreal adventures packed with film and pop-culture references.

items.title: The Sopranos
items.plot: New Jersey mob boss Tony Soprano starts seeing a psychiatrist after panic attacks, and struggles to balance the pressures of running a criminal organization with the demands of his family.

won: 2000 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
nominated: 2001 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2002 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2003 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2005 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: The West Wing
items.plot: President Josiah Bartlet and his dedicated senior staff navigate political crises, legislative battles, scandals and personal sacrifices inside the White House over two terms in office.

won: 2001 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
nominated: 2000 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2002 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2003 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2004 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: Coupling
items.plot: Six London friends in their thirties dissect sex, dating and relationships in frank, intricately structured comic stories, centered on the on-off romance of Steve and Susan.

items.title: Curb Your Enthusiasm
items.plot: Seinfeld co-creator Larry David plays a version of himself in Los Angeles, whose rigid ideas about social etiquette spark escalating feuds and awkward disasters in largely improvised episodes.

won: 2003 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
nominated: 2006 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy

items.title: Fighting Spirit
items.plot: Bullied, shy teenager Ippo Makunouchi is rescued by a boxer and discovers his own talent for the sport, training at the Kamogawa gym and battling a series of tough opponents on his path toward the featherweight title.

items.title: Band of Brothers
items.plot: The true story of Easy Company, 506th Parachute Infantry Regiment, from paratrooper training in Georgia through D-Day, Market Garden, the Battle of the Bulge and the capture of Hitler's Eagle's Nest.

items.title: Justice League
items.plot: Superman, Batman, Wonder Woman, the Flash, Green Lantern, Martian Manhunter and Hawkgirl unite as the Justice League to defend Earth from alien invasions, supervillains and cosmic threats in multi-part adventures.

items.title: Samurai Jack
items.plot: A samurai prince is flung into a dystopian future ruled by the shape-shifting demon Aku he was about to defeat, and wanders this strange world searching for a way back to the past to undo Aku's evil.

items.title: Six Feet Under
items.plot: After their father's sudden death, the dysfunctional Fisher family takes over his Los Angeles funeral home, confronting grief, sexuality, relationships and their own mortality as each episode opens with a death.

won: 2002 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
nominated: 2003 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2004 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: The Blue Planet
items.plot: David Attenborough narrates a pioneering natural history of the world's oceans, from coral reefs and coastlines to the open sea and the alien life of the deep, revealing many behaviors never filmed before.

items.title: The Office
items.plot: A documentary crew films the employees of a paper company's branch in Slough, where deluded manager David Brent thinks he is a beloved entertainer while his staff endure awkwardness and boredom.

won: 2004 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
nominated: 2007 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy

items.title: Trailer Park Boys
items.plot: A documentary crew follows petty criminals Ricky, Julian and Bubbles in a Nova Scotia trailer park as they hatch hare-brained money-making schemes, clash with the drunken park supervisor and keep ending up in jail.

items.title: Firefly
items.plot: In 2517, Captain Mal Reynolds, a veteran of the losing side of a civil war, leads the crew of the transport ship Serenity through odd jobs and smuggling on the frontier, while hiding two fugitives wanted by the Alliance.

items.title: Foyle's War
items.plot: During and after World War II, quiet, principled Detective Chief Superintendent Christopher Foyle investigates murders and wartime crimes such as black-marketeering and espionage, first in Hastings and later as an MI5 agent.

items.title: Still Game
items.plot: Lifelong friends and pensioners Jack and Victor live in a Glasgow tower block, spending their days trading insults and gossip with their neighbors and the regulars at the local pub.

items.title: The Shield
items.plot: Corrupt LAPD detective Vic Mackey and his elite Strike Team fight gangs and drug dealers by any means necessary, including theft and murder, while trying to stay a step ahead of investigators and their own colleagues.

won: 2003 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: The Wire
items.plot: Baltimore police and drug dealers face off in a sprawling portrait of an American city, as each season expands to the docks, city hall, the schools and the newspaper to show how institutions fail the people they serve.

items.title: Top Gear
items.plot: A rebooted BBC motoring show mixing car reviews, celebrity laps of the test track and ambitious, often absurd road-trip challenges. The hosts' banter and elaborate stunts turned it into one of the most-watched factual programmes in the world.

items.title: Arrested Development
items.plot: After his father is arrested for fraud, level-headed Michael Bluth tries to hold together his spoiled, self-absorbed and deeply dysfunctional wealthy family. Narrated documentary-style, it layers running gags and callbacks across seasons.

nominated: 2004 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
2005 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy

items.title: Battlestar Galactica
items.plot: When the Cylons, machines created by humanity, launch a devastating surprise attack on the Twelve Colonies, an aging warship and a ragtag civilian fleet become the last remnants of the human race. This two-part miniseries launched the reimagined saga.

setting.place: The Twelve Colonies and deep space

nominated: 1979 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: Chappelle's Show
items.plot: Comedian Dave Chappelle hosts a sketch show that skewers race, celebrity and pop culture, mixing filmed sketches with musical performances before a live audience. Its characters and parodies became cultural touchstones before Chappelle walked away mid-production.

items.title: Peep Show
items.plot: Two mismatched flatmates in Croydon, uptight loan manager Mark and lazy would-be musician Jeremy, stumble through jobs, relationships and their own neuroses. Shot from the characters' point of view, with their inner monologues heard aloud.

items.title: QI
items.plot: A comedy panel quiz where points are awarded for interesting answers rather than correct ones, and obvious-but-wrong answers are penalised. Each series works through a letter of the alphabet, mixing obscure facts with improvised banter.

items.title: The Venture Bros.
items.plot: A washed-up boy-genius scientist, his two naive sons and their violent bodyguard stumble through adventures against costumed villains. The animated series parodies 1960s adventure cartoons while building an elaborate, melancholy mythology about failure.

items.title: Battlestar Galactica
items.plot: After a Cylon attack wipes out the Twelve Colonies, the warship Galactica leads a fleet of survivors in search of the mythical planet Earth. Pursued by machines that can now look human, the fleet wrestles with paranoia, politics and faith.

items.title: Deadwood
items.plot: In the lawless mining camp of Deadwood in the 1870s, former lawman Seth Bullock and ruthless saloon owner Al Swearengen clash as the settlement edges toward civilisation. Real historical figures mingle with fictional ones in famously profane, Shakespearean dialogue.

nominated: 2005 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: House
items.plot: Brilliant but misanthropic diagnostician Dr. Gregory House and his team tackle baffling medical cases at a New Jersey teaching hospital. House's addiction to painkillers and contempt for rules strain everyone around him.

nominated: 2008 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2009 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2010 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: Justice League Unlimited
items.plot: The Justice League expands into a huge roster of DC heroes operating from an orbital Watchtower, taking on threats from rogue gods to a shadowy government conspiracy. The animated sequel to Justice League spotlights lesser-known heroes alongside Superman, Batman and Wonder Woman.

items.title: Long Way Round
items.plot: Actor Ewan McGregor and friend Charley Boorman ride BMW motorcycles from London to New York heading east, crossing Europe, Kazakhstan, Mongolia and Siberia. Bad roads, border bureaucracy and exhaustion test their friendship along the way.

setting.place: London to New York via Asia and Alaska

items.title: Monster
items.plot: Japanese surgeon Kenzo Tenma saves a young boy's life in West Germany, only to learn years later that the child has grown into a charismatic serial killer. Framed for murder, Tenma pursues him across Germany and Czechia.

items.title: Samurai Champloo
items.plot: A teahouse waitress recruits two quarrelling swordsmen, a wild vagabond and a disciplined ronin, to help her find a mysterious samurai who smells of sunflowers. Their road trip across Edo-era Japan blends sword fights with hip-hop music and anachronisms.

items.title: Sarabhai V/S Sarabhai
items.plot: In an upper-class Mumbai household, snobbish matriarch Maya Sarabhai clashes with her middle-class daughter-in-law Monisha while her husband and sons trade wisecracks. The family's eccentric members fuel a satire of Indian class pretensions.

items.title: Avatar: The Last Airbender
items.plot: In a world where people can bend water, earth, fire and air, a young monk awakens from a century frozen in ice to learn he is the Avatar. With new friends he must master all four elements and stop the Fire Nation's war of conquest.

items.title: Gintama
items.plot: In an alternate Edo-era Japan conquered by aliens, lazy ex-samurai Gintoki runs an odd-jobs business with two young companions. Absurd parody episodes alternate with serious sword-fighting arcs.

items.title: It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia
items.plot: Five selfish, delusional friends run an Irish pub in Philadelphia and drag each other into increasingly depraved schemes. The gang never learns a lesson, making them among the most awful people on television.

items.title: Rome
items.plot: Two Roman soldiers, a disciplined centurion and a brawling legionary, find their lives entangled with the great figures of the late Republic, from Julius Caesar's rise to Octavian's triumph. Politics and street life unfold side by side.

nominated: 2006 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: The Boondocks
items.plot: Brothers Huey and Riley Freeman move from Chicago's South Side to a white suburb with their grandfather. Radical young Huey and wannabe-gangster Riley become vehicles for sharp satire of American race, politics and pop culture.
items.source: The Boondocks comic strip by Aaron McGruder

items.title: The Office
items.plot: A documentary crew follows the employees of the Scranton branch of the Dunder Mifflin paper company, led by well-meaning but cringe-inducing manager Michael Scott. Workplace pranks, office romance and petty rivalries fill their days.

nominated: 2009 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
2010 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy

items.title: The Thick of It
items.plot: Hapless ministers and advisers at a fictional British government department lurch from crisis to crisis under the eye of foul-mouthed spin doctor Malcolm Tucker. A handheld, improvised-feeling satire of modern politics and media management.

items.title: Code Geass: Lelouch of the Rebellion
items.plot: In an alternate world where the Holy Britannian Empire has conquered Japan, exiled prince Lelouch gains the power to command anyone to obey him. As the masked Zero, he leads a rebellion against the empire that betrayed him.

items.title: Death Note
items.plot: Brilliant student Light Yagami finds a notebook that kills anyone whose name is written in it and sets out to purge the world of criminals. An eccentric detective known only as L begins a battle of wits to unmask him.
items.source: Death Note by Tsugumi Ohba and Takeshi Obata

items.title: Dexter
items.plot: Miami police blood-spatter analyst Dexter Morgan leads a secret life as a serial killer who only targets murderers, following a code taught by his adoptive father. Keeping his double life hidden from colleagues and family grows ever harder.
items.source: Darkly Dreaming Dexter by Jeff Lindsay

nominated: 2009 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2010 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2011 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: Friday Night Lights
items.plot: In the small football-obsessed town of Dillon, Texas, coach Eric Taylor, his wife Tami and their high-school players navigate pressure, ambition and growing up. The game is a lens on family, class and community.
items.source: Friday Night Lights (2004 film) and H.G. Bissinger's book

items.title: Planet Earth
items.plot: A landmark nature documentary that surveys the planet habitat by habitat, from poles and deserts to deep oceans and caves. Groundbreaking high-definition and aerial filming captures rarely seen animal behaviour, narrated by David Attenborough.

items.title: The IT Crowd
items.plot: Two socially inept tech-support workers toil in the basement of a London corporation under a new manager who knows nothing about computers. Their attempts to deal with the outside world go spectacularly wrong.

items.title: Flight of the Conchords
items.plot: Two deadpan New Zealand musicians try to make it in New York with the help of an inept manager and their only fan. Their misadventures regularly break into parody songs in a range of musical styles.

items.title: Mad Men
items.plot: Charismatic advertising creative director Don Draper hides a secret past while thriving on Madison Avenue in the 1960s. The series follows his colleagues and family as social change sweeps through the decade.

won: 2008 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2009 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2010 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
nominated: 2011 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: Naruto: Shippuden
items.plot: After years of training, an older Naruto Uzumaki returns to his ninja village to rescue his friend Sasuke and face the Akatsuki, a group hunting tailed beasts like the one sealed inside him. The conflict builds to a world-spanning ninja war.

setting.place: The Hidden Leaf Village and ninja lands

items.title: Breaking Bad
items.plot: A mild-mannered Albuquerque chemistry teacher diagnosed with terminal cancer starts cooking methamphetamine with a former student to provide for his family. His transformation into a ruthless drug kingpin drags everyone around him down.

won: 2014 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
nominated: 2013 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: Sons of Anarchy
items.plot: Jax Teller, vice president of an outlaw motorcycle club in a small California town, begins questioning the club's violent path while his mother and stepfather fight to keep control. Loosely echoes Hamlet.

items.title: Apocalypse: The Second World War
items.plot: A six-part history of World War II assembled entirely from archival footage, much of it restored and colourised. It traces the conflict from the rise of Nazism to the atomic bombings through the experiences of soldiers and civilians.

items.title: Archer
items.plot: Sterling Archer, a vain and reckless secret agent, works for a dysfunctional intelligence agency run by his domineering mother. Later seasons reinvent the format with new settings and genres.

items.title: Ezel
items.plot: Betrayed by his closest friends and the woman he loved, Ömer is imprisoned for a crime he did not commit. Years later he returns to Istanbul with a new face and identity, Ezel, to take revenge.
items.source: The Count of Monte Cristo by Alexandre Dumas

items.title: Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood
items.plot: After a failed attempt to resurrect their mother costs them dearly, alchemist brothers Edward and Alphonse Elric search for the Philosopher's Stone to restore their bodies. Their quest uncovers a conspiracy reaching the top of their military state.

items.title: Life
items.plot: A BBC natural history series exploring the strategies animals and plants use to survive and reproduce, from hunting and courtship to raising young. Each episode focuses on a group such as mammals, insects or primates, narrated by David Attenborough.

items.title: Parks and Recreation
items.plot: Relentlessly optimistic bureaucrat Leslie Knope and her eccentric co-workers in the parks department of small-town Pawnee, Indiana, try to make local government work. Shot mockumentary-style, it grows into a warm ensemble comedy.

nominated: 2014 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy

items.title: Adventure Time
items.plot: Young Finn and his shape-shifting dog Jake roam the candy-coloured Land of Ooo, fighting monsters and helping princesses. Beneath the whimsy lies a post-apocalyptic world whose history and melancholy deepen over the series.

items.title: Behzat Ç: An Ankara Detective Story
items.plot: Hard-drinking, rule-breaking homicide detective Behzat Ç. and his team investigate murders in Ankara while he struggles with grief and his own demons. Gritty and darkly funny, it painted an unvarnished portrait of Turkish society.
items.source: Behzat Ç. novels by Emrah Serbes

items.title: Boardwalk Empire
items.plot: As Prohibition begins, Atlantic City treasurer Enoch 'Nucky' Thompson runs the town's bootlegging trade while balancing politicians and rising gangsters such as Al Capone and Lucky Luciano. Power struggles grow bloodier through the 1920s.

won: 2011 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
nominated: 2012 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2013 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: Downton Abbey
items.plot: The aristocratic Crawley family and their servants at a Yorkshire country house face upheaval from the Titanic's sinking through the First World War and the 1920s. Questions of inheritance, romance and class shape both upstairs and downstairs.

nominated: 2013 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2014 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2015 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: Justified
items.plot: Quick-draw U.S. Marshal Raylan Givens is reassigned to his home turf in rural eastern Kentucky, where he faces criminals including his old friend Boyd Crowder. Each season pairs cases of the week with a larger crime war.
items.source: Fire in the Hole by Elmore Leonard

items.title: Louie
items.plot: Comedian Louis C.K. plays a fictionalised version of himself, a divorced father of two working the New York stand-up circuit. Loosely connected vignettes mix stand-up, awkward encounters and surreal, melancholy storytelling.

items.title: Regular Show
items.plot: Mordecai the blue jay and Rigby the raccoon work as groundskeepers at a park but would rather do anything else. Their attempts to slack off routinely spiral into surreal, supernatural adventures.

items.title: Sherlock
items.plot: A modern-day reimagining of Arthur Conan Doyle's detective, with Sherlock Holmes using phones and blogs to solve crimes across contemporary London alongside army doctor John Watson. Each feature-length episode updates a classic story.
items.source: Sherlock Holmes stories by Arthur Conan Doyle

items.title: The Great British Baking Show
items.plot: Amateur bakers gather in a tent in the English countryside to compete in weekly challenges judged by expert bakers. One contestant leaves each week until a winner is crowned in a famously gentle, good-natured competition.

items.title: Through the Wormhole
items.plot: Morgan Freeman hosts a science series exploring big questions about the universe, consciousness, time and existence. Scientists explain cutting-edge research on topics from black holes to the nature of God.

items.title: Young Justice
items.plot: Teenage sidekicks of DC's greatest heroes form a covert team to take on missions the Justice League cannot. Over the seasons they confront a shadowy conspiracy known as the Light and an alien invasion.

items.title: Black Mirror
items.plot: A dark anthology of standalone stories about the unintended consequences of technology, from social media and surveillance to virtual reality and artificial intelligence. Each episode has a new cast, setting and often a twist.

items.title: Frozen Planet
items.plot: A BBC nature series following a year in the Arctic and Antarctic, showing how polar bears, penguins, wolves and whales survive the extremes of the planet's coldest places. Narrated by David Attenborough, it ends with a look at the changing climate.

items.title: Game of Thrones
items.plot: Noble houses scheme and wage war for the Iron Throne of the Seven Kingdoms of Westeros, while an exiled princess builds an army across the sea. Far to the north, an ancient threat stirs beyond a colossal wall of ice.
items.source: A Song of Ice and Fire by George R.R. Martin

nominated: 2012 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2015 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2016 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2017 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2018 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: Human Planet
items.plot: A BBC documentary series showing how people in every kind of environment, from deserts and jungles to oceans, mountains and cities, have adapted to survive. Narrated by John Hurt, it captures traditional skills and dramatic relationships with nature.

items.title: Hunter X Hunter
items.plot: Young Gon Freecss sets out to become a Hunter, an elite licensed adventurer, hoping to find the father who left him. With friends he faces deadly exams, criminal syndicates and monstrous creatures in a world governed by a power system called Nen.

items.title: Impractical Jokers
items.plot: Four lifelong friends from Staten Island dare each other to carry out embarrassing hidden-camera challenges on unsuspecting members of the public. Whoever refuses the most dares faces a humiliating punishment.

items.title: Leyla and Mecnun
items.plot: Mecnun, born on the night of an eclipse, falls for Leyla, born the same night, and spends years trying to win her. The absurdist comedy follows him and his eccentric friends and family in an Istanbul neighbourhood, full of surreal jokes and pop-culture references.

items.title: Steins; Gate
items.plot: Self-proclaimed mad scientist Rintaro Okabe and his friends accidentally invent a device that can send text messages to the past. Their experiments draw the attention of a sinister organisation and trap Okabe in a struggle to undo the consequences.

items.title: The Bridge
items.plot: A body found exactly on the border midway across the Øresund Bridge forces socially awkward Swedish detective Saga Norén to team up with a Danish counterpart. Each season follows a new cross-border case that reveals more of Saga's past.

items.title: Endeavour
items.plot: A prequel to Inspector Morse following the young Endeavour Morse as a detective constable and later sergeant in 1960s and 1970s Oxford. Under the guidance of DI Fred Thursday he solves murders while battling corruption and his own loneliness.
items.source: Inspector Morse novels by Colin Dexter

items.title: Farouk Omar
items.plot: A large-scale historical drama about the life of Umar ibn al-Khattab, the second caliph of Islam, from his early opposition to the Prophet Muhammad through his conversion and rule. Produced for Ramadan, it depicts the rise of the early Islamic state.

items.title: Gravity Falls
items.plot: Twins Dipper and Mabel Pines spend the summer with their great-uncle in a strange Oregon town, where a mysterious journal leads them into supernatural mysteries. Hidden codes and a sinister dream demon build toward a world-threatening finale.

items.title: Line of Duty
items.plot: Officers of AC-12, a police anti-corruption unit, investigate fellow officers suspected of misconduct, while slowly uncovering links between organised crime and senior ranks. Each series centres on a new suspect, interrogated in famously tense interview scenes.

setting.place: Unnamed English city (filmed in Birmingham and Belfast)

items.title: The Eric Andre Show
items.plot: A deliberately chaotic parody of public-access talk shows in which host Eric André destroys his set, ambushes celebrity guests and pulls disturbing street pranks. The anarchic format turns awkwardness into comedy.

items.title: The Newsroom
items.plot: Cable news anchor Will McAvoy and his staff set out to produce serious, principled journalism against corporate and ratings pressure. Each episode revolves around real news events from 2010 onward.

nominated: 2013 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: Africa
items.plot: David Attenborough guides a journey across Africa's deserts, savannahs, jungles and coasts, revealing remarkable wildlife behaviour. A final episode looks at the continent's future and conservation challenges.

items.title: Attack on Titan
items.plot: Humanity survives behind massive walls to escape giant man-eating Titans. When a Titan breaches the wall and destroys his home, young Eren Yeager joins the military to fight back, and the truth behind the Titans turns out to be darker than anyone imagined.
items.source: Attack on Titan by Hajime Isayama

items.title: House of Cards
items.plot: Passed over for Secretary of State, ruthless congressman Frank Underwood and his equally ambitious wife Claire scheme their way toward the presidency. Frank often addresses the audience directly as he manipulates and destroys rivals.
items.source: House of Cards (BBC, 1990) and Michael Dobbs' novel

nominated: 2014 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2015 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: Mahabharat
items.plot: A lavish Hindi retelling of the ancient Indian epic, following the rivalry between the Pandava and Kaurava cousins over the throne of Hastinapur. It culminates in the great war of Kurukshetra and Krishna's teachings in the Bhagavad Gita.

items.title: Nathan for You
items.plot: Comedian Nathan Fielder, playing an awkward version of himself, offers struggling small businesses outlandish marketing schemes and follows real people as they try them. The deadpan docu-comedy blurs reality and performance.

items.title: Peaky Blinders
items.plot: In Birmingham after the First World War, cunning gang leader Tommy Shelby and his family's razor-wielding gang expand their empire from illegal betting into politics and beyond. Ambition pulls them into clashes with rivals, police and fascists.

items.title: Rick and Morty
items.plot: Alcoholic super-scientist Rick Sanchez drags his anxious grandson Morty on dangerous adventures across dimensions and planets. The animated series mixes absurd sci-fi concepts with dark family comedy and existential nihilism.

items.title: BoJack Horseman
items.plot: BoJack, a washed-up anthropomorphic horse who starred in a 1990s sitcom, tries to revive his career and find meaning in Hollywoo. Behind the animal puns, the series examines depression, addiction and self-destruction.

items.title: Cosmos: A Spacetime Odyssey
items.plot: Astrophysicist Neil deGrasse Tyson continues Carl Sagan's journey through the universe, explaining the history of science and the cosmos with a 'Ship of the Imagination' and animated stories of scientific pioneers. A follow-up season, Possible Worlds, aired in 2020.

items.title: Detectorists
items.plot: Two friends and amateur metal detectorists, Andy and Lance, spend their days searching the Essex countryside for buried treasure while dealing with relationships, rival clubs and life's small disappointments. A gentle, warm comedy.

items.title: Fargo
items.plot: An anthology of darkly comic crime stories set mostly in the snowy Upper Midwest, each season following ordinary people pulled into violence and deception across different decades. Inspired by the Coen brothers' film, with subtle links between seasons.

items.title: Gomorrah
items.plot: Ciro Di Marzio, a trusted soldier of the Savastano Camorra clan in Naples, and Genny, the boss's son, are drawn into a brutal power struggle. Alliances form and collapse as rival factions fight over drug territory.

items.title: Haikyuu!!
items.plot: Short but determined Shoyo Hinata joins his high school volleyball team, where he must partner with Tobio Kageyama, a gifted setter and former rival. Together they push Karasuno High toward the national tournament.

items.title: Happy Valley
items.plot: Police sergeant Catherine Cawood, raising her grandson after her daughter's suicide, confronts the man she holds responsible when he resurfaces in her West Yorkshire valley. Crime and family trauma intertwine across three series.

items.title: Last Week Tonight with John Oliver
items.plot: John Oliver hosts a weekly satirical news show that recaps current events and devotes a long main segment to an in-depth investigation of an under-covered issue. Its deep dives often spark real-world reactions.

items.title: Over the Garden Wall
items.plot: Half-brothers Wirt and Greg are lost in a strange forest called the Unknown and try to find their way home with the help of a talkative bluebird. Along the way they meet odd folk and are stalked by a sinister creature, the Beast.

items.title: Silicon Valley
items.plot: Socially awkward programmer Richard Hendricks invents a revolutionary compression algorithm and tries to build a startup around it with his misfit friends. They battle tech giants, investors and their own incompetence.

nominated: 2015 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
2016 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy

items.title: True Detective
items.plot: An anthology crime drama in which each season follows different detectives investigating a disturbing case, exploring their obsessions and the dark secrets of the places they police. Settings range from Louisiana to Alaska.

items.title: Your Lie in April
items.plot: Former piano prodigy Kosei Arima stopped playing after his mother's death left him unable to hear his own music. A free-spirited violinist, Kaori Miyazono, pulls him back into performing and changes his life.
items.source: Your Lie in April by Naoshi Arakawa

items.title: Better Call Saul
items.plot: Years before Breaking Bad, small-time lawyer Jimmy McGill struggles to go straight in Albuquerque while living in his brilliant brother's shadow. His slide toward becoming the crooked attorney Saul Goodman unfolds alongside fixer Mike Ehrmantraut's entry into the drug trade.

nominated: 2023 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: Critical Role
items.plot: A group of professional voice actors play an ongoing Dungeons & Dragons campaign led by game master Matthew Mercer, streamed live in long weekly sessions. Their improvised adventures in the fantasy world of Exandria grew into a media franchise.

items.title: Daredevil
items.plot: Blind lawyer Matt Murdock fights injustice in court by day and as a masked vigilante in Hell's Kitchen by night, using heightened senses. His war on crime pits him against kingpin Wilson Fisk.

items.title: Making a Murderer
items.plot: A documentary series filmed over a decade following Steven Avery, a Wisconsin man exonerated after 18 years in prison who is then charged with murder, along with his nephew Brendan Dassey. It scrutinises police conduct and the justice system.

items.title: Mr. Robot
items.plot: Elliot Alderson, a cybersecurity engineer with social anxiety and dissociative episodes, is recruited by a mysterious anarchist hacker group to bring down the corporation he is paid to protect. Reality and delusion become hard to separate.

won: 2016 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: Narcos
items.plot: The rise and fall of Colombian drug lord Pablo Escobar and the Medellín cartel, told partly through DEA agents hunting him, followed by the fight against the Cali cartel. Real archival footage mixes with dramatisation.

nominated: 2016 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: One Punch Man
items.plot: Saitama trained so hard he can defeat any opponent with a single punch, leaving him bored and unrecognised as a hero. He joins the Hero Association alongside his cyborg disciple Genos while monsters keep attacking.
items.source: One-Punch Man by ONE and Yusuke Murata

items.title: Reply 1988
items.plot: Five families living in the same Seoul alleyway in 1988 share daily joys and hardships, while their teenage children navigate friendship, school and first love. A nostalgic comedy-drama with a mystery about who one heroine will marry.

items.title: Schitt's Creek
items.plot: After losing their fortune, the ultra-wealthy Rose family is forced to move to Schitt's Creek, a small town they once bought as a joke. Living in a motel, the spoiled family slowly grows closer and finds a real home.

won: 2021 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy

items.title: TVF Pitchers
items.plot: Four friends in Delhi quit their corporate jobs to chase a startup dream. The series follows the pitches, investors, egos and setbacks of building a company from nothing in India's young startup scene.

items.title: Taskmaster
items.plot: Five comedians compete in a series of absurd, open-ended tasks set by Alex Horne, with the imperious Greg Davies judging and scoring their efforts. Each series crowns a winner who takes home a golden bust of Davies' head.

items.title: The Bureau
items.plot: An undercover French intelligence officer returns from six years in Syria to the DGSE's Bureau of Legends, which runs agents under false identities. He secretly resumes a forbidden relationship from his cover life, setting off a dangerous chain of compromises.

items.title: The Expanse
items.plot: Centuries from now, with Earth, Mars and the Belt locked in a cold war, a detective and an ice-hauler crew are drawn into a conspiracy around a missing woman. What they uncover threatens the fragile peace and humanity itself.

items.title: The Jinx: The Life and Deaths of Robert Durst
items.plot: Filmmaker Andrew Jarecki investigates real-estate heir Robert Durst, long suspected in his wife's disappearance and two later killings, after Durst agrees to be interviewed. A follow-up season covers the aftermath and his eventual trial.

items.title: Atlanta
items.plot: Earn, a Princeton dropout scraping by in Atlanta, tries to manage his cousin's rising rap career as Paper Boi. The show mixes surreal comedy and sharp social observation about race, money and fame.

won: 2017 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy

items.title: Fleabag
items.plot: A sharp, self-destructive young woman runs a struggling guinea-pig café in London while dealing with grief, family friction and messy relationships. She shares her thoughts directly with the audience, hiding the pain behind her jokes.

won: 2020 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy

items.title: Mob Psycho 100
items.plot: Shigeo 'Mob' Kageyama is a shy middle schooler with enormous psychic powers he tries to keep bottled up. Working for a fraudulent spiritual con man, he battles spirits and espers while trying to become a normal, better person.

items.title: Planet Earth II
items.plot: David Attenborough narrates a return to the natural world a decade after Planet Earth, using new camera technology to film wildlife on islands, mountains, jungles, deserts, grasslands and in cities.

items.title: Stranger Things
items.plot: In 1980s Hawkins, Indiana, a boy vanishes, and his friends, family and the local police chief uncover secret government experiments, a girl with psychokinetic powers and a monstrous parallel dimension.

nominated: 2017 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2018 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: The Crown
items.plot: A dramatized chronicle of Queen Elizabeth II's reign, from her marriage and accession through the political crises, family scandals and public pressures of the following decades.

won: 2017 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2021 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
nominated: 2018 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2020 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2023 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2024 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: The Grand Tour
items.plot: After leaving Top Gear, Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May travel the world testing cars, bickering and undertaking elaborate road trips and stunts, later shifting to feature-length specials.

items.title: This Is Us
items.plot: The Pearson family's story unfolds across several timelines, following parents Jack and Rebecca raising their triplets and the grown siblings navigating love, loss, addiction and identity decades later.

nominated: 2017 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2018 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: Anne with an E
items.plot: Orphan Anne Shirley, imaginative and talkative, is mistakenly sent to elderly siblings on Prince Edward Island who wanted a boy. She wins over the community of Avonlea while confronting prejudice and her own traumatic past.
items.source: Anne of Green Gables (L. M. Montgomery)

items.title: Black Sun
items.plot: In interwar Belgrade, a police inspector investigates a murder that draws him into a web of crime, occultism, Russian émigrés and high politics across the Balkans. Also known as Shadows Over the Balkans.

items.title: Blue Planet II
items.plot: David Attenborough guides viewers through the world's oceans, from coral reefs and kelp forests to the deep sea, revealing newly filmed animal behavior and the threats facing marine life.

items.title: Dark
items.plot: When children start disappearing in the small German town of Winden, four intertwined families uncover a time-travel conspiracy linking generations across 33-year cycles.

items.title: Mindhunter
items.plot: In the late 1970s, two FBI agents and a psychologist interview imprisoned serial killers to understand how they think, pioneering criminal profiling while applying it to active cases.
items.source: Mind Hunter: Inside the FBI's Elite Serial Crime Unit (John Douglas, Mark Olshaker)

setting.place: Quantico, Virginia and across the USA

items.title: The Chosen
items.plot: A dramatization of the life of Jesus told largely through the eyes of those who met and followed him, including fishermen, a tax collector and outcasts, building toward the events of his final days.

items.title: The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel
items.plot: In 1958 New York, a seemingly perfect Upper West Side housewife discovers a gift for stand-up comedy after her marriage falls apart, and pursues a career in a male-dominated world.

won: 2018 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
nominated: 2019 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
2020 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy

items.title: The Vietnam War
items.plot: Ken Burns and Lynn Novick trace the Vietnam War from its colonial roots to the fall of Saigon, combining archival footage with testimony from Americans and Vietnamese on all sides.

items.title: Twin Peaks
items.plot: Twenty-five years after the events in Twin Peaks, FBI agent Dale Cooper's fate is tied to a sinister doppelgänger, as strange happenings spread from the town to Las Vegas, New Mexico and beyond.

setting.place: Twin Peaks, Washington; Las Vegas; South Dakota

items.title: Bluey
items.plot: Bluey, an energetic six-year-old Blue Heeler puppy, turns everyday family life in Brisbane into imaginative games with her little sister Bingo and her endlessly patient parents.

items.title: Derry Girls
items.plot: Four Catholic schoolgirls and one English boy cousin navigate teenage life in 1990s Derry, Northern Ireland, while the Troubles and the peace process play out around their chaotic families.

items.title: Mr Inbetween
items.plot: Ray Shoesmith is a Sydney hitman and enforcer who also tries to be a good father, boyfriend, brother and friend. The show balances deadpan humor with sudden violence as his two lives keep colliding.

items.title: My Brilliant Friend
items.plot: Elena and Lila meet as girls in a poor Naples neighborhood in the 1950s. The series traces their intense, competitive lifelong friendship as their lives diverge through education, marriage and Italy's turbulent decades.

items.title: My Mister
items.plot: A weary middle-aged engineer and a hardened young temp worker in debt, initially hired to dig up dirt on him, slowly form an unlikely bond that helps each of them heal.

items.title: Persona
items.plot: A retired courthouse clerk newly diagnosed with Alzheimer's sets out to take revenge for long-buried wrongs before he forgets them, while a determined gendarmerie investigator tries to connect a series of killings.

items.title: Pose
items.plot: In late-1980s and 1990s New York, members of the Black and Latino LGBTQ ball culture, many of them trans women, build chosen families and compete for glory while facing poverty, prejudice and the AIDS crisis.

nominated: 2019 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2022 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: Succession
items.plot: Aging media mogul Logan Roy controls a global conglomerate, and his four children scheme, betray and jockey with each other for a chance to take over the family business.

won: 2020 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2022 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2024 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
