items.title: The Haunting of Hill House
items.plot: Siblings who grew up in a notorious haunted mansion are forced together as adults after a tragedy, confronting the ghosts of their past both literal and emotional, in a story told across two timelines.
items.source: The Haunting of Hill House (Shirley Jackson)

items.title: Yeh Meri Family
items.plot: A nostalgic look at a middle-class Indian family through the eyes of its kids during a single summer, capturing everyday squabbles, school worries and family warmth. Later seasons follow new families in the same spirit.

items.title: Yellowstone
items.plot: Rancher John Dutton fights to protect the largest contiguous cattle ranch in the United States from developers, a neighboring Native American reservation and politicians, often through brutal means, while his family fractures.

items.title: Chernobyl
items.plot: A dramatization of the 1986 Chernobyl nuclear disaster, following the scientists, workers and officials who fought to contain the catastrophe and expose the lies that caused it.

items.title: Crash Landing on You
items.plot: A South Korean heiress paragliding accident leaves her stranded in North Korea, where a stoic army officer hides and protects her. As he tries to get her home, they fall in love across a hostile border.

items.title: Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba
items.plot: After demons slaughter his family and turn his sister Nezuko into one of them, Tanjiro Kamado joins the Demon Slayer Corps to find a cure for her and hunt down the demon who started it all.
items.source: Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba (Koyoharu Gotouge)

items.title: Greatest Events of WWII in Colour
items.plot: Colorized archival footage and expert commentary recount ten pivotal events of World War II, from the Battle of Britain and Pearl Harbor to D-Day and the fall of Berlin.

items.title: Gullak
items.plot: Narrated by the family's piggy bank, slice-of-life stories follow the Mishras, a middle-class family in a small North Indian town, through squabbles over money, school, jobs and neighbors.

items.title: Kota Factory
items.plot: Shot in black and white, the series follows 16-year-old Vaibhav as he moves to Kota, India's coaching hub, to prepare for the IIT entrance exam, guided by a beloved physics teacher known as Jeetu Bhaiya.

items.title: Our Planet
items.plot: Narrated by David Attenborough, this documentary showcases the planet's habitats, from frozen worlds to jungles and high seas, highlighting how climate change and human activity threaten the wildlife that depends on them.

items.title: Primal
items.plot: In a savage prehistoric world, a caveman and a Tyrannosaurus, both having lost their families, form an unlikely bond to survive. Told almost entirely without dialogue through stark, violent animation.

items.title: The Boys
items.plot: In a world where superheroes are corporate-owned celebrities who abuse their power, a group of vigilantes known as the Boys sets out to expose and take down the corrupt heroes of Vought International.

items.title: The Family Man
items.plot: Srikant Tiwari appears to be an ordinary middle-class family man but secretly works as an agent for a covert counterterrorism cell, struggling to balance national-security missions with a marriage and kids who know nothing.

items.title: The Mandalorian
items.plot: After the fall of the Empire, a lone Mandalorian bounty hunter on the galaxy's lawless fringes takes on a job that leaves him protecting a mysterious child strong in the Force.

setting.period: Far-future-like galaxy (5 years after Return of the Jedi)

nominated: 2021 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: Vinland Saga
items.plot: In 11th-century Northern Europe, young Thorfinn joins the band of the mercenary who killed his father, hoping for a duel to avenge him. Years of war and slavery later, he searches for a life beyond violence.

items.title: What We Do in the Shadows
items.plot: A documentary crew follows four centuries-old vampire roommates and their long-suffering human familiar on Staten Island as they bumble through modern life, petty feuds and supernatural politics.
items.source: What We Do in the Shadows (2014)

items.title: When They See Us
items.plot: Five Black and Latino teenagers from Harlem are wrongly accused and convicted of a 1989 assault in Central Park. The series follows their coerced confessions, trials, imprisonment and eventual exoneration.

items.title: All Creatures Great & Small
items.plot: In 1937, young Scottish vet James Herriot joins an eccentric practice in the Yorkshire Dales, winning over skeptical farmers and finding a home and love as war approaches.

items.title: How to with John Wilson
items.plot: Anxious New York documentarian John Wilson sets out to give practical advice on mundane topics, like making small talk or covering furniture, but his secretly filmed footage spirals into strange, touching portraits of the city's people.

items.title: Jujutsu Kaisen
items.plot: High schooler Yuji Itadori swallows a cursed finger to save his friends and becomes host to the powerful demon Sukuna. He enrolls at a school for jujutsu sorcerers to track down the remaining fingers and fight curses.

items.title: Panchayat
items.plot: An engineering graduate with few options reluctantly takes a job as secretary of a village panchayat office in remote Uttar Pradesh, slowly getting drawn into the villagers' lives and local politics.

items.title: Scam 1992: The Harshad Mehta Story
items.plot: A dramatization of stockbroker Harshad Mehta's rise from a Mumbai chawl to Dalal Street's 'Big Bull', and the 1992 securities scam exposed by journalist Sucheta Dalal that brought him down.

items.title: Smiling Friends
items.plot: Two employees of a small company dedicated to making people smile, the cheerful Charlie and the anxious Pim, take on bizarre jobs across a surreal, often disturbing world.

items.title: Ted Lasso
items.plot: An upbeat American college football coach with no soccer experience is hired to manage a struggling London Premier League club, winning over cynics with relentless optimism and kindness.

nominated: 2021 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
2022 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy
2024 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy

items.title: The Last Dance
items.plot: Built around unreleased footage of the Chicago Bulls' 1997-98 season, the series chronicles Michael Jordan's career and the Bulls' dynasty through interviews with players, coaches and rivals.

items.title: The Queen's Gambit
items.plot: Orphaned in the 1950s, Beth Harmon discovers a prodigious talent for chess in a Kentucky orphanage. She rises through the competitive chess world while battling addiction and loneliness.
The Dutton family leaves Tennessee and joins a wagon train of immigrants heading west across the Great Plains, facing disease, bandits and brutal terrain on their way to a new home in Montana.

items.title: Arcane
items.plot: Sisters Vi and Jinx are torn apart amid rising tension between the wealthy, utopian city of Piltover and its oppressed undercity, Zaun, as magical technology threatens to ignite war.

items.title: As If
items.plot: Three friends, the sarcastic Yılmaz, the would-be intellectual İlkkan and the naive Ersoy, stumble through absurd everyday situations in this deadpan Turkish comedy of mostly self-contained episodes. Original title: Gibi.

items.title: Aspirants
items.plot: Three friends who once prepared together for India's demanding civil services exam in Delhi's Old Rajinder Nagar reunite years later, as past choices and rivalries resurface.

items.title: Clarkson's Farm
items.plot: Jeremy Clarkson attempts to run his 1,000-acre farm in the Cotswolds himself, battling weather, bureaucracy, local councils and his own inexperience with help from young farmhand Kaleb Cooper.

items.title: Dopesick
items.plot: The story of America's opioid epidemic, from Purdue Pharma's aggressive marketing of OxyContin to a small Appalachian mining town ravaged by addiction and the investigators trying to hold the company accountable.

items.title: Invincible
items.plot: Mark Grayson, the teenage son of Omni-Man, the world's most powerful superhero, develops powers of his own, only to discover his father's legacy is far darker than he imagined.
items.source: Invincible (Robert Kirkman, Cory Walker, Ryan Ottley)

items.title: It's a Sin
items.plot: In 1981, a group of young gay men and their friends move to London and share a flat, celebrating newfound freedom just as the AIDS epidemic begins to devastate their community over the following decade.

items.title: The Beatles: Get Back
items.plot: Peter Jackson restores hours of footage from January 1969 to show the Beatles writing and rehearsing new songs under a tight deadline, culminating in their famous rooftop concert.

items.title: Alchemy of Souls
items.plot: In the fictional kingdom of Daeho, a powerful sorceress trapped in a weak body by a forbidden soul-swapping spell becomes servant and secret teacher to a young nobleman with a mysterious past.

items.title: Andor
items.plot: Five years before Rogue One, thief Cassian Andor is drawn into the nascent rebellion against the Empire, as the series charts how ordinary people are radicalized and how the Rebel Alliance took shape.
items.source: Rogue One: A Star Wars Story

items.title: Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War
items.plot: Soul Reaper Ichigo Kurosaki and the Soul Society face their deadliest enemy yet when the Wandenreich, an army of Quincy led by Yhwach, launches a surprise invasion in the manga's final arc.

items.title: Rocket Boys
items.plot: A dramatization of the lives of scientists Homi J. Bhabha and Vikram Sarabhai, who laid the foundations of India's nuclear and space programs in the decades around independence.

items.title: Severance
items.plot: Employees at Lumon Industries undergo a procedure that splits their memories between work and home. Office worker Mark and his colleagues begin to uncover what their company is really doing.

nominated: 2023 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama
2026 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: The Offer
items.plot: Novice producer Al Ruddy fights studio executives, the mob and creative clashes to get Francis Ford Coppola's The Godfather made at Paramount in the early 1970s.

items.title: The Rehearsal
items.plot: Nathan Fielder helps ordinary people prepare for life's difficult moments by building elaborate, hyper-detailed simulations to rehearse them, an experiment that grows stranger and more personal as it goes.

items.title: Blue Eye Samurai
items.plot: In Edo-period Japan, Mizu, a mixed-race sword master disguised as a man, sets out on a quest for revenge against the four white men in Japan, one of whom fathered her.

items.title: Frieren: Beyond Journey's End
items.plot: After the hero's party defeats the Demon King, the long-lived elf mage Frieren outlives her companions. Regretting how little she knew them, she sets out on a new journey to understand people.
items.source: Frieren: Beyond Journey's End (Kanehito Yamada, Tsukasa Abe)

items.title: Sapne Vs Everyone
items.plot: Two young men in Mumbai, a small-town aspiring actor and a middle-class engineer dreaming of a real-estate business, chase their ambitions against financial pressure, family expectations and the city's harsh realities.

items.title: Scavengers Reign
items.plot: Survivors of a damaged interstellar freighter crash on a strange, beautiful and deadly alien planet and must navigate its interconnected ecosystem while trying to reach the ship and get home.

items.title: Twinkling Watermelon
items.plot: A hearing high schooler from a deaf family, secretly in love with playing guitar, travels back to 1995 through a mysterious music shop and meets his own parents as teenagers.

items.title: Shōgun
items.plot: In 1600 Japan, English navigator John Blackthorne is shipwrecked and becomes entangled in the power struggle of Lord Toranaga, who is maneuvering against rival regents, with the Christian noblewoman Mariko as interpreter.

won: 2025 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: The Penguin
items.plot: After the flooding of Gotham City, scarred gangster Oz Cobb makes a ruthless play to seize control of the criminal underworld, clashing with Sofia Falcone, daughter of the late crime boss.

items.title: X-Men '97
items.plot: Picking up after the 1990s animated series, the X-Men grieve Professor X and face new threats under Magneto's leadership, as tensions between mutants and humans boil toward catastrophe.

items.title: Dexter: Resurrection
items.plot: Having survived his apparent death, Dexter Morgan heads to New York City to find his estranged son Harrison and soon crosses paths with a secret club of wealthy serial-killer enthusiasts.

items.title: Heated Rivalry
items.plot: Two rival young hockey stars, Canadian Shane Hollander and Russian Ilya Rozanov, carry on a secret years-long relationship while competing at the top of professional hockey.

items.title: Takopi's Original Sin
items.plot: An innocent octopus-like alien named Takopi comes to Earth to spread happiness and befriends Shizuka, a girl suffering from bullying and neglect, but his cheerful gadgets can't fix the darkness in her life.

items.title: The Pitt
items.plot: Each season covers a single 15-hour shift in a Pittsburgh hospital's overwhelmed emergency department, with each episode an hour in real time, as Dr. Robby and his staff juggle patients, trainees and their own burnout.

won: 2026 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: When Life Gives You Tangerines
items.plot: On Jeju Island in the 1950s, spirited poet-dreamer Ae-sun and steadfast Gwan-sik fall in love. The series follows their life together through hardship and joy across the decades of modern Korea.

setting.place: Jeju Island and Seoul, South Korea

items.title: A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms
items.plot: About a century before Game of Thrones, the towering, kind-hearted hedge knight Ser Duncan the Tall and his young squire Egg wander Westeros, entering a tournament where Targaryen politics complicate everything.
items.source: Tales of Dunk and Egg: The Hedge Knight (George R. R. Martin)

items.title: Shōgun
items.plot: An English navigator shipwrecked in feudal Japan in 1600 is drawn into the power struggle of the warlord Toranaga, learning the language and customs of a culture that at first seems utterly alien to him.

won: 1981 Golden Globes · Best Television Series – Drama

items.title: Roots
items.plot: A remake of the landmark saga: Kunta Kinte is captured in West Africa and enslaved in Virginia, and his descendants carry his story through generations of bondage toward the end of the Civil War.
items.source: Roots: The Saga of an American Family

items.title: Monster
items.plot: A true-crime anthology from Ryan Murphy and Ian Brennan, each season dramatizing a notorious American killer and the people around them, beginning with Jeffrey Dahmer and continuing with the Menendez brothers and Ed Gein.

items.title: The Bob Newhart Show
items.plot: Comedian Bob Newhart's half-hour variety show, built around his deadpan telephone monologues plus sketches and guest stars. It won an Emmy and a Peabody yet was cancelled after one season.
